Maximian.fact: His ambitions were purely military; he left politics to Diocletian. The Christian rhetor Lactantius suggested that Maximian shared Diocletian's basic attitudes but was less puritanical in his tastes, and took advantage of the sensual opportunities his position as emperor offered.

Maximian.fact: The rulers discussed matters of politics and war in secret, and they may have considered the idea of expanding the imperial college to include four rulers (the Tetrarchy).
